data.description:
## Problem

External-integration code (third-party SDKs, webhook contracts, OAuth flows, retry / idempotency patterns, off-pattern usage of vendor APIs) produces a class of bugs that general code review reliably misses. The same novelty that makes integrations risky — they sit on the boundary where our code meets a vendor's contract — also means existing reviewers lack the prior-art context to recognize deviations from established usage. Bugs ship; we discover them in production or via vendor escalation.

This epic introduces a code-review overlay that compares integration code against captured prior-art references using a tiered evidence rubric, so deviations surface during review rather than after merge.

## Solution shape

A new classifier-dispatched code-reviewer sub-agent (`dso:code-reviewer-integration-prior-art`) that runs in parallel with the existing `dso:code-reviewer-*` family. The agent:

1. Detects in-scope integration code in the diff (markers, SDK imports, or parent-epic tag).
2. Reads a `## Integration Prior-Art Manifest` section from the epic ticket (or walks to it via parent hierarchy for bugs).
3. Applies a tiered evidence rubric (A / B / C) comparing the diff's integration code against the manifest's references.
4. Emits findings into `reviewer-findings.json` with a typed `evidence` field carrying tier, references, provenance, and SDK skew metadata.
5. Findings flow through the existing autonomous-resolution loop (R1–R5) keyed by severity — no special handling.

Manifests live in the epic ticket. No global registry, no cross-epic lookup. Each epic carries its own self-contained reference set; past tickets are historical reference data for brainstorm authors only.

## Strategic decisions (locked during brainstorm)

| # | Dimension | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reviewer agent | New named sub-agent `dso:code-reviewer-integration-prior-art`. Classifier-dispatched in parallel with other reviewers. Findings written to `reviewer-findings.json` via the standard schema plus a new optional `evidence` field. Disable knob: `review.integration_prior_art.enabled` (default true) in `dso-config.conf`. |
| 2 | Evidence rubric (3 tiers) | **Tier A — documented_canonical**: official doc + ≥1 corroborator → severities 1–3. **Tier B — undocumented_quirk**: ≥3 independent OSS consumers → severities 1–3. **Tier C — documented_unreferenced**: official doc only, no corroborator → **always severity 4 (minor, non-blocking)**. |
| 3 | Resolution flow | Uniform R1–R5 by severity. Tier is evidence metadata only; the resolution loop branches on severity, not tier. The reviewer chooses severity; tier informs but doesn't override that choice. |
| 4 | Manifest location | `## Integration Prior-Art Manifest` section in the epic ticket description. Self-contained per epic; no cross-epic registry. The reviewer never reaches across epics — past Stripe epics are NOT consulted for a new Stripe epic's review. Historical tickets remain searchable as reference data for brainstorm authors who pull patterns forward into the new epic. |
| 5 | Manifest format | Per-provider `### <provider>` sub-section under the top-level header. Sub-section contains an `SDK: <name> v<version> — last verified: <date>` line followed by three labelled markdown lists: **Official Documentation**, **OSS Consumers**, **Other**. The three labelled lists map 1:1 to the rubric's tier inputs (Tier A/C need entries under Official Documentation; Tier B needs ≥3 entries under OSS Consumers). Multi-provider epics carry multiple `###` sub-sections under one top-level header. |
| 6 | Reference source + failure mode | Primary: brainstorm-captured manifest in the epic. Fallback on primary fetch failure: WebSearch with structured queries derived from `(provider, sdk, sdk_version, construct_under_review)`. Hard-fail the review cycle only when both primary AND WebSearch recovery yield no usable references. Provenance tagged on every reference (`source: "manifest" \| "websearch"`) so audits can see substitution. |
| 7 | Scope detection / classifier signal | Hybrid. Classifier dispatches the new agent when ANY of: (a) any file in the diff contains a `# dso:integration <provider>` marker comment (or language equivalent), (b) any file in the diff imports an SDK whose provider appears in the current epic's manifest, (c) the parent ticket's tag set includes `external-integration`. Any one signal fires → dispatch. |
| 8 | Planning enforcement (marker AC) | `dso:implementation-plan` emits an Acceptance Criterion on any task whose parent epic carries `external-integration` (or whose preplanning manifest cites an SDK from the epic's manifest), requiring file-level marker comments on every new or modified integration file. Test files and pure data fixtures exempt. Marker syntax: `# dso:integration <provider>` (Python/shell), `// dso:integration <provider>` (JS/TS/Go/Rust/Java), `<!-- dso:integration <provider> -->` (HTML/Markdown). |
| 9 | Manifest authorship lifecycle | `/dso:brainstorm` writes the manifest when it has signal during epic ideation. Preplanning runs a gate at decomposition: if the epic is tagged `external-integration` but the manifest section is missing or empty for a declared provider, preplanning auto-generates a `recipe:integration-manifest-spike` task as the first task of the epic. Downstream integration-touching stories are blocked-by the spike via normal ticket linking. Mid-epic discovery of a new provider re-triggers preplanning to add another spike. Spike's acceptance criteria: section populated with one `### <provider>` sub-section per declared provider, SDK + version line present, ≥1 entry under **Official Documentation** for each. |
| 10 | Sprint bug auto-tagging | When `/dso:sprint` creates a bug ticket during a sprint run (test failure, runtime failure, recipe failure, debug-everything escalation), sprint inspects the failure context. If the stack trace references a file with a `# dso:integration <provider>` marker OR imports an SDK in the current epic's manifest OR the bug was triggered by a prior-art reviewer finding, sprint applies tag pair `external-integration` + `provider:<name>` at bug-create time. Detection is mechanical (no LLM call). Sprint passes the tags through to the `create-bug` skill at ticket-create time. |
| 11 | Bug-fix workflow | Reviewer walks the bug ticket's parent hierarchy looking for an epic ancestor. **Epic ancestor present** → use that epic's manifest (normal mode). **No epic ancestor, bug tagged `external-integration`** → WebSearch-only mode; all references tagged `provenance.source: "websearch"`; rubric still classifies tiers from live-fetched references. **No epic ancestor, no `external-integration` tag** → skip overlay; emit single non-blocking informational notice (`"prior-art overlay skipped: bug <id> has no epic ancestor"`). |
| 12 | Manifest staleness | Reviewer parses SDK version from each `### <provider>` sub-section's `SDK:` line and compares against the SDK version detected in the code's dependency manifest (`pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`, `package.json`, equivalents per language). On MAJOR-version skew → single sev-4 minor finding per provider: `"manifest references <sdk> v<N>; code uses v<M> — references may be stale; consider refreshing the manifest"`. Minor/patch skew ignored. Non-blocking visible nudge. |
| 13 | Finding payload schema | Standard `reviewer-findings.json` shape (path, line, severity, category, description) PLUS a new optional top-level `evidence` field per finding: `{tier: "A"\|"B"\|"C"\|null, references: [{url, type, source}], sdk: {name, version_manifest, version_code}}`. `evidence.tier: null` reserved for meta-findings such as staleness. `references[].type` enum: `"official-doc" \| "oss-consumer" \| "blog" \| "sdk-readme"`. `references[].source` enum: `"manifest" \| "websearch"`. Non-breaking: existing consumers ignore unknown fields. New contract doc: `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/integration-prior-art-finding.md`. |
| 14 | Validation strategy | Ship as a normal classifier-dispatched reviewer. No bespoke golden-diff regression suite; no shadow-mode calibration period. False positives ride the existing autonomous-resolution loop (`TrackerDefenseStore` locally, `GitHubPRDefenseStore` in CI). Iteration trigger: per-category defense rate for `category: "integration-prior-art"` exceeds a configurable threshold (suggested 50%) → team reviews recent defended findings and refines the agent prompt. Quality emerges through real-world iteration on real PRs. |

## Tactical items (resolved at implementation time)

- **Bootstrap content**: none required. Manifests are authored per-epic as integrations are introduced; no global registry to seed.
- **PR comment surfacing**: the typed `evidence` field supports a rich renderer (per-tier grouping, reference list with provenance hyperlinks); specific copy is a one-pass implementation detail.
- **Rubric prompt text**: lives in the new agent's frontmatter / skill file; authored during implementation. Should explicitly state the three-tier rubric, severity mapping, evidence-object shape, and the "emit zero findings if integration code matches established patterns" instruction.
- **Contract doc**: `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/integration-prior-art-finding.md` documenting the typed `evidence` field. Update `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md` if defense-format changes are needed.
- **Multi-language SDK-import detection**: classifier needs to recognize imports per language. Suggested approach: each manifest entry's SDK identifier maps to a per-language import pattern (`stripe-python` → Python `import stripe`; `@stripe/stripe-js` → JS `from "@stripe/stripe-js"`). Pattern table can live in a per-language helper or be derived from the SDK identifier directly during implementation.
- **Configuration keys (new)**: `review.integration_prior_art.enabled` (bool, default true). Document in `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`. Defense-rate iteration threshold (suggested 50%) can be added later if needed.

## Out of scope (explicitly)

- Cross-epic manifest lookup / global integration registry.
- Golden-diff regression suite or shadow-mode calibration.
- Special-cased resolution-loop behavior per tier (e.g., Tier B citation-in-fix requirement).
- TTL-based manifest staleness detection (only major-version skew is in scope).
- Automatic refresh of manifest references (humans / brainstorm do the refresh).

## Touch-points for implementation

These existing skills, agents, and infrastructure pieces will need changes:

- `plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/` — capture references during epic ideation; write `## Integration Prior-Art Manifest` section.
- `plugins/dso/skills/preplanning/` — gate on manifest presence for `external-integration` epics; auto-generate `recipe:integration-manifest-spike` task if missing.
- `plugins/dso/skills/implementation-plan/` — emit marker-comment AC for tasks with `external-integration` scope.
- `plugins/dso/skills/sprint/` — inspect failure context; tag created bugs with `external-integration` + `provider:<name>`.
- `plugins/dso/skills/create-bug/` — accept tag arguments from sprint (already supported via `--tags`; verify path).
- New: `plugins/dso/agents/dso-code-reviewer-integration-prior-art.md` (or wherever the existing reviewer agents live) — the new sub-agent itself.
- Existing review classifier — add dispatch rules for the new agent based on the scope-detection signals.
- `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/integration-prior-art-finding.md` — new contract doc.
- `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md` — document `review.integration_prior_art.enabled`.
- `plugins/dso/docs/AGENTS.md` — register the new named sub-agent.

## References

- Brainstorm session conducted 2026-05-24 on branch `claude/brainstorm-external-integrations-zjn9c`.
- Related contracts: `plugins/dso/docs/contracts/review-defenses.md`, `plugins/dso/docs/CI-INTEGRATION.md`, `plugins/dso/docs/CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md`.
